transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-24
Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morris (Redwood SE), Joanna Lee (Hearthly PM), Marcus Chen (Eng Lead), Priya Rao (Security), Tina Alvarez (Data)
transcript_body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir with Redwood, AE on the account. Happy to run through a hosted API walkthrough — streaming, key params, retry patterns — and show the console + Optimize suggestions. Who wants to kick us off with objectives?
[00:31] Joanna: Yeah thanks Samir. Main thing for us is fast integration for chat on the customer support flow. Need sub-2s median latencies for short replies, and predictable cost. We'll also need to show security folks SOC2 and VPC options.
[01:08] Marcus: And from eng: our traffic baseline is roughly 80 RPS peak for chat, average token length 60, but spikes up to 300 RPS during promos. We want to understand batching and the tradeoffs.
[01:45] Elena: Great, that's helpful. I'll start with a quick API demo — live request/streaming — then jump into console Optimize and the autoscaling / batching knobs. Note: I'll be using a sandbox model; production is identical but metrics differ.
[02:12] (screen share noise) Elena: Alright hitting the generate endpoint in streaming mode. Sequence: we do a chat.message payload, set max_tokens, temperature, and stream=true — you'll see chunked parts come back.
[02:39] Marcus: Quick question, what's the default chunk size on the stream? Is that based on token or byte boundary?
[03:05] Elena: It's token-boundary friendly; we flush after model chunk emits. There's also a stream_heartbeat option to keep connections alive during long sequences.
[03:30] Joanna: And for intermittent network blips, what's the retry story?
[04:02] Samir: Good — we recommend idempotency keys for non-chat endpoints, but for chat we surface a resume token (we call it the continuation cursor) so client can resume from last partial event. If you prefer, can also use short-lived retry windows and rehydrate KV cache to avoid regen from scratch.
[04:36] Priya: Sorry, can you repeat KV cache? Our security folks heard "K V cash" — what is that exactly?
[04:58] Elena: Yeah, sorry audio — KV cache (key-value cache). For chat it stores the model's past-key-values so we don't resend full context to the GPU each request, which speeds up token-gen massively. We do encryption at rest and in transit, and we can configure lifecycle in Private/Dedicated.
[05:31] Tina: How much perf delta are we talking about with KV cache turned on?
[05:55] Elena: Typical improvement is 30-60% per-token latency on longer histories. For short requests (a few tokens) impact is smaller. Optimize can suggest whether to enable prefix caching based on your conversation lengths.
[06:28] Marcus: If we enable batching, how do you preserve low tail latency? Our SLOs are tight.
[06:50] Samir: Two levers: continuous batching (small windows + priority routing) and a fast-path for latency-sensitive short requests. You can split traffic by route — route low-latency requests to reserved capacity or a smaller batch size policy. There's also a token-based preemptive flush.
[07:26] Joanna: Can you show where we tune that in the console?
[07:45] (Elena navigates console) Elena: Sure — here under 'Routes' you can set batching windows, max batch size, and a latency SLO. There's a visual histogram of request size and inferred per-token cost. Optimize will flag routes where switching model or adjusting batch windows reduces cost without breaking SLO. Link: [Console: /quickstart/HEARTHLY-demo] (placeholder).
[08:30] Marcus: I see model variants — what's Redwood's recommendation: larger model with higher quality vs smaller with quantization?
[08:58] Elena: Optimize runs a workload analysis; it recommends quantized variants for high-throughput routes and full-precision for quality-critical routes. You can use canary rollouts per-route to validate.
[09:25] Samir: Also note we have automatic fallback policies — if a chosen model is overloaded we can fallback to a compatible variant or to hosted spare capacity. This helps avoid 503s.
[09:49] Joanna: On the subject of fallbacks, how much quality regression is typical when switching to a quantized model?
[10:12] Elena: Usually small; Optimize gives a delta estimate and suggests example prompts where regressions occur. We also attach per-prompt evals to monitor quality drift.
[10:38] Priya: Security question: for the hosted API, what does the audit trail look like?
[10:59] Samir: We provide request-level logs (token-level redaction options), admin audit logs, and can integrate with your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging. SOC2 artifacts and pen-test reports are in the packet I'll send.
[11:30] Priya: Is there SSO? SAML?
[11:50] Elena: Yes, SAML and OIDC, RBAC maps to groups, and you can restrict console access by IP ranges for extra control.
[12:12] (slight crosstalk) Marcus: Let's talk cost math a bit — do you have examples on console?
[12:34] Elena: Under Optimize -> Cost Explorer we break down token cost by model, route and show estimated $/k tokens. You can simulate switching to a quantized model or enabling prefix cache and see the projected delta.
[13:10] Tina: Is there an API to pull those estimates programmatically?
[13:34] Samir: Yep, Optimize exposes an endpoint you can poll to get cost suggestions and the recommended config bundle. It's useful for automated CI to gate model rollouts.
[14:00] Joanna: Can we get a canned report for our traffic shape?
[14:17] Elena: We'll run an initial analysis in the POC; please share the traffic profile (Marcus/Tina). We'll produce a suggested config and cost/latency projection.
[14:40] Marcus: About retries — if we have partial response and then reconnect, how do we avoid double counting tokens for billing?
[15:02] Samir: Billing is token-accurate; with session resume/continuation cursor we avoid regen. If a request is fully retried, we pro-rate or have hooks to waive tokens for duplicate attempts depending on the situation — details in billing FAQ.
[15:33] Joanna: Demo time — can you intentionally cause a timeout and show retry-resume behavior?
[15:50] (Elena simulates) Elena: I'll throttle the connection... you can see on stream we emit a partial chunk, then the client reconnects with the continuation cursor and we re-send only remaining tokens — so user sees near-continuous output.
[16:40] Marcus: Nice. Any client libraries for handling resume tokens?
[16:55] Elena: We have SDKs in JS, Python that handle stream reconnection, backoff strategies, and resume out-of-the-box.
[17:15] Tina: What's your recommended backoff strategy? Exponential with jitter?
[17:32] Samir: Exactly. Exponential backoff with jitter, cap retry attempts (3-5), and avoid re-sending identical requests without idempotency keys. For streaming, use the resume token first before full retry.
[18:00] Joanna: About data residency — some of our customers are EU-only; can you guarantee EU region for hosted?
[18:23] Samir: Yes, we have EU-hosted regions and can pin customer traffic. For stricter needs, Dedicated or Private deployments are options.
[18:45] Priya: For the POC we need to know where keys are stored — KMS / HSM?
[18:59] Elena: Hosted supports cloud KMS, and for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. I'll include a diagram in the packet.
[19:22] Marcus: Can we talk about a simple rollout plan? Start hosted sandbox, then POC with production-like traffic, then decide Dedicated?
[19:40] Samir: That's our typical flow. For your scale, we recommend a 2-week POC with baseline tracing and a 4-week pilot stage if you want to validate spikes. We'll provide a POC checklist.
[20:05] Joanna: Can you email the checklist?
[20:12] Samir: Yes — action item.
[20:30] (short pause) Elena: I'm going to show Optimize's suggested batch config for your sample workload. It suggests small batch windows (10–20 ms) for chat fast-path and 50–80 ms for high-throughput routes; and to enable prefix caching for multi-turn sessions.
[21:10] Marcus: That small? 10–20 ms window seems low, will that actually accumulate meaningful batches?
[21:30] Elena: It depends on qps. At 80 RPS you get some natural batching; the fast-path will favor immediate dispatch for short replies. The point is to set the policy per route.
[21:50] Joanna: Any gotchas in the console?
[22:05] Elena: Watch the alerting thresholds — if you allow large batches you may see increased p95. Also keep an eye on the cache eviction policy.
[22:28] Priya: For compliance, can we get a retention window for logs and a way to redact PII automatically?
[22:45] Samir: Yes retention configurable per account and token redaction options. We also have eval tooling to detect PII in responses and block exfiltration.
[23:10] Tina: Do you have prebuilt connectors for our CRM? We use Zendesk; want to attach generated replies.
[23:30] Elena: Common pattern: webhook from platform to your backend which posts to Zendesk. We also have a sample integration repo.
[23:50] Marcus: If we hit a model outage, what's SLA and failover steps?
[24:10] Samir: For hosted we have regional fallbacks and multi-model failovers. SLA specifics are in the Dedicated/enterprise contract. For POC we'll define recovery checkpoints.
[24:40] Joanna: Can you outline expected timeline for POC starting next Monday?
[24:57] Samir: If we start Monday, we can spin up sandbox the same day, get telemetry ingest in 2–3 days, run initial Optimize analysis within 5 business days, and have a baseline report within 7.
[25:23] Marcus: Any tokenization quirks with emojis/HTML?
[25:40] Elena: Tokenization can vary; Optimize accounts for real tokenization on target model and will show per-turn token counts. We recommend sanitizing HTML or using structured output to avoid surprise tokens.
[26:05] (short examples demo) Elena: showing a few prompts, adjust temperature and top_p; lower temp reduces variance but also reduces creative phrasing. For deterministic templated replies we recommend temp ~0–0.2.
[26:41] Tina: What about streaming partial generations for UX? Should we stream every token or batch into chunks?
[27:00] Samir: UX decision — streaming every token gives smoothness but higher network chatter. Chunked streaming (e.g., 50–100 chars) reduces chattiness. Resume tokens still work either way.
[27:30] Joanna: Are there any limits we should be aware of in sandbox?
[27:45] Elena: Sandbox limits are soft; production has quota and rate limiting. We'll share quota guidance in the deck.
[28:00] (brief mute/hold) Samir: Ok I want to recap next steps — we'll send SOC2 & security packet, console walkthrough recording, and the POC checklist. Marcus/Tina to share traffic profile. We'll schedule the technical deep-dive for private/VPC options with Priya.
[28:30] Marcus: Sounds good.
[28:40] Joanna: One more quick ask — can you include a sample failure-mode document for our on-call? We need to know how to detect and rollback.
[29:00] Elena: Yes, I'll add the runbook and a couple of rollback playbooks.
[29:20] Priya: For the deep dive, can we include network diagrams and expected firewall rules?
[29:40] Samir: Absolutely.
[30:00] (closing minutes — light banter) Joanna: Thanks everyone, this was super helpful. Marcus, we'll share the profile by Friday.
[30:20] Marcus: Yep.
[30:30] Samir: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet and recording.
[51:55] (meeting ends; residual chatter) Speaker 1: bye everyone
